# regex-literal: regular expressions in source and in configuration.
# character classes and escapes look like packed opaque bytes, and never are.
# known cost: dense regex bodies can clear the entropy gate in configuration and call literals.
# configuration example: `sed_expr = 's/[A-Za-z0-9_-]\{22,\}/<x>/g'`
# and `validate = "^arn:aws:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/[A-Za-z0-9+=,.@_-]+$"`.
# known cost: independent call bodies skip syntax exemptions: let re = Regex::new(r"^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=$").unwrap();
# known cost: independent call bodies skip syntax exemptions: PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?i)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b")
const SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/u;
filter: "^(src|tests)/.*[.](rs|toml)$"
    r"[\x21-\x7e&&[^=]]+={0,2}"
matches = re.findall(r"[A-Z]{2,}_[A-Z0-9_]{4,}", text)
router.get(/^\/api\/v[0-9]+\/orders$/, handler)
assert!(Regex::new(r"^(?:[0-9a-f]{2}:){5}[0-9a-f]{2}$").is_match(mac));
exclude_pattern: '(?x) ^ (?: vendor | third_party ) / .* $'
    grep_pattern = "[[:xdigit:]]{32}[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+"
